added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no baseline_suite or after_suite gate log (the reviewed node's gate is a live install on intr26-2, not a pytest suite), so the added-failure count was not taken and is stored as unmeasured rather than as a measured zero

findings.text: follow-on: the gate log's header stamps revision b24db7ec8b97 but neither run it records measured that revision (the first rerun at 09:56:11Z built imas_alambic-0.1.dev5956+g9cc44e5a1 and the final run at 09:58:54Z built ...dev5957+gcf788ff5b), so the log's first line does not name the revision it ran at; the log also ends at '== done' with no EXIT= line, so the '-> EXIT=0' the manifest quotes is not on the log it cites, and a mis-named redirect artifact 'imasdb-install.log 2>&1' sits beside it holding the earlier attempt.

follow-on: the installer spells the layout name maps/current in its seed (ln -sfn "$STAGE/bundle" "$IMASDB/maps/current") rather than taking it from imas-alambic config as the plan requires, though it reads and validates the config names immediately after at lines 171-180; the manifest records the seed as the forced workaround for config's MachineMapError, so one layout name still has a second owner in the installer.

follow-on: the fence clause 'find IMASDB -perm -o+w prints nothing' cannot be satisfied at this layout because a symlink's own mode is 0777 and maps/current is a symlink; the node correctly substituted 'find "$IMASDB" -not -type l -perm -o+w' and documented it (packages/imas-alambic/install/imasdb.sh:212-219), so the fence literal should be corrected to the real-files-and-directories form.

item_verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit against base 49c9fabc: b24db7ec adds the installer, 9cc44e5a seeds the map search path before the config read and folds the interpreter under the folder, cf788ff5 adds --force so a rerun replaces an existing tool executable, 1061ce22 adds the evidence fragment; the net change is +346 lines across the two files.
item_verdicts.done_when: Every clause of the dispatched evidence fence reproduces in the run log (final run 09:58:54Z): /home/SharedFolder/d240044 is mode 1755; no directory under IMASDB lacks others r-x; no file lacks others r; the no-write check over real files and directories prints nothing; uv pip show reports imas-alambic installed, not editable, from a wheel; --version exits 0 both with the python/3.12 site-packages on PYTHONPATH and with it unset; uv pip check reports 24 packages compatible; config with no IMAS_ALAMBIC_* reports maps IMASDB/maps/current, ids_root IMASDB/ids and machine jt-60sa; the old ~/imas-alambic top level was listed, removed and shown gone. Two clauses are not literally met and are recorded as findings: the fence literal 'find IMASDB -perm -o+w prints nothing' cannot hold because a symlink's own mode is 0777, so the node substituted a symlink-excluding check, and the installer spells maps/current once in its seed.
item_verdicts.goal: The node's goal is one command that installs imas-alambic from wheels into the shared IMASDB folder on intr26-2; at head 1061ce22 packages/imas-alambic/install/imasdb.sh (271 lines) builds the engine and nova-cocos wheels with uv build, pulls ghcr.io/simon-mcintosh/imas-alambic-jt60sa:2026.10.07 with oras and the gh token, relays them over ssh jt-60sa, installs the engine as a uv tool on a uv-managed CPython 3.12 under IMASDB/tools, writes the launcher, seeds the map search path, places the bundle under maps/2026.10.07 with current pointing at it, opens the tree read-only to others, checks it, and removes the old ~/imas-alambic.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read; it records the four commits, the two installer reruns and the earlier MachineMapError attempt, the live install path, the bundle digest, the tool environment, and one follow-on (config raising MachineMapError on a descriptorless map search-path entry); every quoted result I checked matches the log on disk except the log's own stamped revision, see finding.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The manifest declares three write paths (packages/imas-alambic/install/imasdb.sh, the evidence fragment, and a figures directory); git diff --stat 49c9fabc..1061ce22 lists exactly two files, packages/imas-alambic/install/imasdb.sh (+271) and docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-facility-mint/jtfm-imasdb-install.html (+75), both inside the declared scope, and the figures directory was correctly not written because the dispatched done-when names no figure.

justifications.durability: No committed test exercises packages/imas-alambic/install/imasdb.sh (git grep at head finds none under tests/); the script's own checks at lines 197-262 measure the installed state on intr26-2 and pass whatever the script's logic does, so a regression that removed the seed, the nice wrapper or the removal guard would not redden any committed test.
justifications.evidence: The run log /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261007T081209804162-jtfm-imasdb-install/logs/imasdb-install.log records each check's real output for the final run, but its header stamps the stale revision b24db7ec and it carries no EXIT= line, and the substituted symlink-excluding no-write check means one fence literal is unmet.
justifications.fit: The installer is idiomatic bash with set -euo pipefail and clear section headers (packages/imas-alambic/install/imasdb.sh:27,56) and carries no plan, ticket or version identifiers.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The installer at packages/imas-alambic/install/imasdb.sh:1-271 delivers the one-command install and every dispatched clause reproduces in the run log; the findings above name the two clauses not literally met.
justifications.reuse: The diff adds no duplicate capability: it reads the layout names from imas-alambic config (packages/imas-alambic/install/imasdb.sh:171-180) so settings.py stays their owner, and reuses the existing uv, oras and ssh tooling.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 49c9fabc..1061ce22 lists only the two declared paths (packages/imas-alambic/install/imasdb.sh and the evidence fragment), with the declared figures directory correctly left unwritten.
